approach: Write docs/design/jev-code-health.md in the section style of hestia.md and scope-guard.md (purpose; how Jev is called, citing defaults-loop.md section 6 and 6.1; five questions each in a fixed table of state, options, criteria, threshold, effect; shadow period and exit rule; scoring by landing-record evidence; fit with deterministic code-health (request 20261026-042558-5p65, described as planned), Hestia D129, scope guard D127; cost per landing; alternatives; risks; build plan of one-producer-run jobs; open points). Append proposed D130 at the end of docs/decisions.md and one CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased/Changed. No code or config.

decisions.choice: Five typed choice questions (one-thing-or-several, adds-coupling, module-placement, god-object-drift, duplicates-existing-logic), each a `choice` type with a `none`/neutral option, so p_top (defaults-loop.md 6.1) is the threshold input. Thresholds are numeric starting values labeled estimates (for example 0.85 to request a structural pass, 0.70 for a status finding), to be set from shadow calibration.
decisions.reason: Matches the section 6 calling convention (state, questions map with type/instructions/criteria) and the brief's named questions; choice questions give a probability per option.

rejected.why: p_top is not the threshold input for booleans and the module-placement question has several options.

rejected.option: Line counts and function length only
rejected.why: The request says line counts cannot judge what a function does; they stay as the deterministic floor.

decisions.choice: Judge per changed function for one-thing and duplicates, per changed file for coupling, god-object drift and placement; the state is a bounded excerpt (hunk plus up to a stated number of lines of context, capped bytes) plus context (path, module list, import lines, size trend), never whole files or records of other jobs.
decisions.reason: Bounds tokens and cost, keeps one call per unit; mirrors defaults-loop 5 rule that only stored fields go to Jev.

rejected.option: One call per file with all functions
rejected.why: Larger state, mixed verdicts, harder to score a single function.
A 5,000-line file would exceed any bounded cost.

decisions.choice: Effects are graded: below the finding threshold nothing; at or above it a status finding; a structural-pass request via 20261026-042558-5p65 only when the deterministic measure also trips (or after shadow exit and a measured precision). In shadow mode every effect is 'record only'.
decisions.reason: Jev never acts alone, consistent with D90/D92 (Jev in shadow, code decides) and the scope guard's rules-first stance.

rejected.why: A false positive costs a producer run; unproven precision.

rejected.option: Block landing on a confident answer
rejected.why: The check is advisory; the scope guard and verifier gate.

decisions.choice: Score by later landing records only (no human labels, per the 2026-10-25 addendum): a flagged file is a hit if a later landing within a stated window fixes or reverts it, a rejection or failed check names it, or its churn (lines changed per landing) is above the repo median; a recommended split is a hit if it lands and the file's churn over the next window drops against the prior window. Compare against a deterministic baseline (largest or most-churned file) to show lift. Exit rule: at least N answers per question and precision above the baseline by a stated margin on two consecutive windows, N and margin estimates.
decisions.reason: Observable later events, computable from records, as Sri asked.

rejected.why: Contradicts the addendum: evidence labels Jev.

rejected.option: Score by a stronger model's opinion

decisions.choice: Cost per landing = calls x $0.00001 with the call count an explicit estimate (for example about 8 changed functions plus 3 changed files times the applicable questions, about 25 to 40 calls, so about $0.0003 to $0.0004, plus an optional escalation call per low-confidence answer per defaults-loop 6.2). Shown with a worst-case cap on calls per landing.
decisions.reason: Evidence default: the number is calls times the stated price, labeled estimate; the per-call price is the request's, not measured.

rejected.why: Orders of magnitude costlier than Jev.

decisions.choice: Append D130 'proposed' to docs/decisions.md with alternatives (line-count only; Jev per file vs per function; model-only reviewer; act immediately without shadow). Avoid the words the decision parse treats as supersession phrases ('supersedes', 'amends', 'superseded by') so decision-links.toml needs no new link.
decisions.reason: decisions.rs parses those phrases (backtest.rs PHRASES) and decision-links.toml lists hits by line number; appending after D129 leaves existing lines and the pinned prefix (PINNED_LEN 230046) unchanged.

rejected.option: Edit existing entries or insert mid-file
rejected.why: The append-only test hashes the prefix and a prior job was rejected for inserting inside another decision (D128).

files.purpose: The design: five questions, shadow period and scoring, fit with deterministic code-health, Hestia and scope guard, cost per landing, alternatives, build plan.
Append D130 (proposed) at the end after D129, with Provenance bullet; no existing byte changes.
Add one bullet under [Unreleased] / Changed for the Jev code-health design and proposed D130.

steps: Read docs/design/hestia.md sections 5 and 9 and scope-guard.md sections 5 and 13 to copy their layout, and docs/records.md for landing-record field names.

Write docs/design/jev-code-health.md: 1 purpose and what Jev is (for outsiders); 2 calling convention citing defaults-loop.md section 6 and 6.1/6.2; 3 the five questions, each with state (excerpt bound and context), options, criteria, numeric threshold, effect; 4 shadow period, record format, exit rule; 5 scoring by evidence from landing records with measurement windows and a deterministic baseline; 6 fit with deterministic code-health (planned, 20261026-042558-5p65), Hestia, scope guard; 7 cost per landing (calls x $0.00001, estimate labeled, cap); 8 alternatives; 9 risks and open points; 10 build plan.

Build plan in the doc (each sized for one producer run, with files and a test): J1 shadow record format and fake-Jev fixtures; J2 state builder (bounded excerpt and context) with tests; J3 Jev client call and question definitions in shadow, using the fake; J4 scorer from landing records; J5 status display of findings and the exit-rule report; J6 effect wiring (status finding, then structural-pass request) after exit.
Append D130 to the end of docs/decisions.md: Status proposed, Case, Decision (proposed), Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance; list the build jobs; use no supersession phrase.
Add a CHANGELOG.md bullet under [Unreleased] / Changed.
Run cargo test --locked, cargo fmt --all --check and clippy to confirm nothing else changed.

risks.risk: D130 text triggers the supersession parser or breaks the append-only/Provenance test.
risks.mitigation: Append only after D129 ending with a Provenance bullet; avoid 'supersedes', 'amends', 'superseded by'; run cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Thresholds and call counts are invented numbers.
risks.mitigation: Label every one as an estimate to be set from shadow calibration; only the $0.00001 price is quoted from the request.

risks.risk: Doc cites planned or unseen things as existing.
risks.mitigation: Call the code-health check 'planned'; cite hestia.md, scope-guard.md, D127, D129 which were seen.

risks.risk: Doc grows too long or vague for Sri to judge.
risks.mitigation: Use one fixed table per question and a short build plan of about six jobs each tagged one producer run with files and a test.

risks.risk: Jev answers may leak other jobs' data.
risks.mitigation: State is limited to the bounded excerpt and path context; follow defaults-loop section 5 rule of no logs or outcomes sent.

demonstrations.method: Read the finished doc and check the five question sections each carry state, options, criteria, a numeric threshold and effect; a grep confirms the five headings and field labels.
demonstrations.observes: Five question sections, each with State, Options, Criteria, Threshold (a number between 0 and 1) and Effect (status finding, structural-pass request via 20261026-042558-5p65, or nothing).

demonstrations.method: Read the shadow-period section and the scoring section for the exit rule and the two measured events with their landing-record fields and windows.
demonstrations.observes: Shadow period defined as record-only; exit rule with numbers; flagged-file-breaks-or-churns and split-lands-and-churn-drops each with how it is computed from landing records.

demonstrations.method: Read the fit and cost sections for citations of docs/design/hestia.md, docs/design/scope-guard.md, the planned code-health check, and a calls x $0.00001 table with the call count labeled estimate.
demonstrations.observes: Links to hestia.md and scope-guard.md, D129 and D127 named, cost arithmetic shown and marked estimate.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff of decisions.md for a single appended D130 marked proposed with alternatives and Provenance, and the doc's build plan jobs each saying sized for one producer run with files and a test or demonstration.
demonstrations.observes: One new entry '## D130 · ... (proposed)' with Status: proposed, Alternatives, Provenance; build-plan jobs each with 'one producer run', files, test.

demonstrations.method: List changed files and read the CHANGELOG diff.
demonstrations.observes: Only docs/design/jev-code-health.md, docs/decisions.md, CHANGELOG.md changed (decision-links.toml unchanged because no new supersession phrase); CHANGELOG has an Unreleased entry for the design.

demonstrations.method: Run the full test suite, which includes the decisions.md append-only/provenance test and the decision-links backtest checks.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, including the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to; this fails if D130 lacks a Provenance bullet, has a lower id, or alters the pinned prefix.
demonstrations.fails_without: A D130 entry missing '- **Provenance:**', inserted mid-file, or containing a bare 'supersedes/amends' phrase would fail the decision-log test or the link backtest.

open_questions: docs/decision-links.toml is listed as an expected deliverable but not in the request's Files line; the plan leaves it unchanged because appended text with no supersession phrase adds no hit. Modify it only if a backtest hit appears.

Which landing-record fields give per-file churn and later breakage were not checked in records code; the doc must name them as to be confirmed by build job 1, and the producer should read docs/records.md for names.
The 20261026-042558-5p65 check is not built or in the snapshot; its measures and thresholds are cited from the request text only (not seen in the repository).
Whether /v1/evaluate answers several questions per call is still unprobed (defaults-loop.md section 6); cost assumes one call per question and notes the saving if batching works.
